title: The bright extragalactic ALMA redshift survey (BEARS) I: redshifts of bright gravitationally lensed galaxies from the Herschel ATLAS
question: Measure spectroscopic redshifts, CO line widths, CO luminosities, and magnification factors for bright gravitationally lensed submillimeter galaxies selected from the Herschel ATLAS South Galactic Pole field.

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image ALMA visibilities, subtract continuum, and re-image cubes
recipe.method: Pipeline/manual calibration in CASA 5.6.1, initial imaging with tclean using natural weighting and Hogbom deconvolver, visual identification of spectral lines, visibility continuum subtraction, and re-imaging with manually adjusted channel widths.
key_parameters: natural weighting, standard gridder, Hogbom deconvolver, pixel scale 2.0/0.5/0.3 arcsec, image size 100x100/240x240 pixels

recipe.goal: Extract spectral line fluxes and line widths
recipe.method: Aperture photometry within the image cubes using circular apertures centered on continuum peaks, with manually adjusted aperture radii and frequency channels to maximize flux while keeping detection above 5 sigma.

Calculate all potential redshift solutions from detected line frequencies and use multi-line detections (59 sources) or single-line exclusion of alternative solutions where other lines would have been detected (13 sources) following Bakx et al. (2020).
assumptions: Adjacent CO spectral lines typically have similar integrated line fluxes, allowing exclusion of redshift solutions for strong single-line detections

recipe.goal: Derive apparent CO(1-0) luminosities and lensing magnification factors
recipe.method: Calculate apparent CO luminosities from the lowest available CO transition using Equation 3 of Solomon & Vanden Bout (2005), convert to CO(1-0) using median SMG brightness temperature ratios from Bothwell et al. (2013), and infer magnification factors from the vertical offset relative to a fit to the unlensed L'_CO(1-0) vs FWHM relation.
assumptions: Spatially flat LambdaCDM cosmology with H0 = 67.4 km s^-1 Mpc^-1 and Omega_M = 0.315
Median SMG brightness temperature ratios from Table 4 of Bothwell et al. (2013) apply for excitation correction
Gravitational magnification depends only on lensing geometry and is independent of velocity width

recipe.goal: Compare inferred magnification distribution with galaxy-galaxy strong lensing population models
recipe.method: Adapt the LensPop code (Collett 2015) with a mock submillimetre source catalogue based on Cai et al. (2013) and source sizes from Ikarashi et al. (2015), simulate 10% of the sky for S_500 > 80 mJy and z_source > 2, and compare the cumulative magnification distribution against the CO-inferred magnifications.
key_parameters: Source density 0.011 arcsec^-2, z > 1 (and z_source > 2 subset), S_500 > 80 mJy and 100 mJy, 10% sky area
assumptions: Strong lensing by elliptical galaxies modelled as singular isothermal ellipsoids (SIEs) with source lying within the Einstein radius

answer_key.quantity: Number of galaxies with robust spectroscopic redshifts

evidence.quote: We present spectroscopic measurements for 71 galaxies associated with 62 of the brightest high-redshift submillimeter sources from the Southern fields of the Herschel Astrophysical Terahertz Large Area Survey (H-ATLAS), while targeting 85 sources which resolved into 142.

answer_key.quantity: Number of Herschel fields with robust redshifts

evidence.quote: We find spectroscopic redshifts for one or multiple sources in 62 of the 85 Herschel fields.

We have obtained robust redshift measurements for all sources using the 12-m Array and an efficient tuning of ALMA to optimise its use as a redshift hunter, with 73 per cent of the sources having a robust redshift identification.
The spectroscopic redshifts span a range $1.41<z<4.53$ with a mean value of 2.75
We note that the uncertainty of the spectroscopic redshifts is less than 0.001, however for clarity, we show only three trailing digits in Table 1.
